thread.title: Nasdaq Closer To Bear Market As Fed Sinks Stocks | Investor's Business Daily

author: JUAN CARLOS ARANCIBIA
title: Nasdaq Closer To Bear Market As Fed Sinks Stocks | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks initially climbed on expectations of a Christmas present from the Federal Reserve Wednesday, but the central bank instead sent indexes closer to a bear market with its latest policy move.
X The Fed, as expected, raised the Fed funds rate by a quarter point . Investors did not see as dovish a Fed as they hoped, sending stocks to new lows.
The Nasdaq composite fell 2.2% to its lowest price since Oct. 26, 2017, and at today's low the index fell 19% below its prior high. That's just one percentage point away from what most would consider a bear-market decline. The composite would need to drop to 6506 to reach a 20% drop.
IBD's current market outlook already is "market in correction," which urges investors to be mainly or entirely in cash.
The S&P 500 slid 1.5%, touching its lowest since Sept. 25, 2017. Its overall decline from the Sept. 21 peak is now 15%.
Small caps, already in a bear market, lost 2.2% in the Russell 2000 Wednesday. The Dow Jones industrial average fell 1.5%. Technology components Intel ( INTC ) and Apple ( AAPL ) were some of the weakest names on the Nasdaq, down 4.6% and 3.1%, respectively.
Apple is almost at the lowest levels of the year after undercutting its April low. Nike ( NKE ) slid more than 3% to a seven-month low.
Volume rose from Tuesday's totals, according to preliminary data. Losing stocks led gainers by a 14-5 ratio on the NYSE and Nasdaq.
Fed policymakers reportedly expect two more rate hikes in 2019 . That's down from a prior estimate of three, but that wasn't enough to calm a jittery Wall Street. Stocks rallied Nov. 28, when Fed Chairman Jerome Powell said rates are close to a normalized level.
The Fed said in its statement Wednesday it sees risks "roughly balanced" and noted strong U.S. job growth, consumer spending and a modest slowing in business investment. The central bank said it would monitor global economic activity, an area of concern for portfolio managers.
Concerns about the global economy were evident in FedEx 's ( FDX ) latest earnings report. The airfreight company missed profit expectations and gave a forecast below estimates as it announced cost cuts to offset slowing business abroad.
Although the company sees the U.S. economy still solid, "our international business weakened during the quarter, especially in Europe," said CEO Frederick Smith. Global trade has slowed, he warned.
